Q: How do prompt versions, examples and output contracts support reproducible behavior?
A:
A prompt is part of a versioned application contract, including instructions, example selection, context formatting and expected outputs. Examples should demonstrate the intended rule and difficult boundaries rather than leak held-out answers or contradict the instructions.

Structured output needs runtime validation and a bounded repair policy; natural-language instructions do not establish valid types. Compare prompt changes on a stable evaluation set and important slices before release. Preserve enough request metadata to reproduce a failure without unnecessarily retaining private content.
Why: A prompt example allowing an unsupported refund can outweigh a vague instruction to follow policy. Correct the example and test both ordinary eligibility and the excluded case instead of merely adding more emphatic wording.
Risk: Unversioned prompt edits make regression diagnosis and rollback difficult.
Trade: Clear short contracts often outperform accumulating contradictory instructions.
Try: Version a prompt and run the same normal, exclusion and insufficient-evidence cases before promotion.
